# Installation {#sec-install}

## Package

Install `sconjoint` from GitHub. It contains C++ code, so it needs a compiler: Xcode command-line
tools on macOS, Rtools on Windows, or a standard build toolchain on Linux.

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("xuyiqing/sconjoint")
```

The package needs R 4.1 or later and four packages: `Rcpp`, `withr`, `digest`, and `spacefillr`
(scrambled Sobol points for numerical integration). The book's figures use base R graphics.

```{r}
#| label: load
library(sconjoint)
packageVersion("sconjoint")
```

Two datasets ship with the package, `gs2020` [@graham2020democracy] and `br2017`
[@ballard2017structure]. `sc_example_data()` turns each into the paper's model inputs.

```{r}
#| label: data-list
data(package = "sconjoint")$results[, c("Item", "Title")]
```

## Saved fits

Fitting the model at the paper's settings takes hours. Most of the time goes to each held-out
respondent's information (@sec-inference), not to training the network. The paper's fold states
are saved in two files:

| File | Application | Taste factors | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gs_q3.rds` | Graham and Svolik (2020) | 3 | about 43 MB |
| `br_q4.rds` | Ballard-Rosa, Martin and Scheve (2017) | 4 | about 21 MB |

The files are too large for the package. They are a separate download, to be published with the
package release. For each of the five folds, a file holds what `sc_estimate()` needs and the fold's
network and covariate scaling. It also holds the respondent ids, groups, folds, the validation
respondents (used to stop training early), and a checksum that `sc_load()` verifies.

@sec-gs, @sec-br, @sec-inference and @sec-respondents read the files from the folder in the option
`sconjoint.fits`. The default is `fits` in the working directory. For another folder, set the
option first:

```{r}
#| label: fits-option
#| eval: false
options(sconjoint.fits = "~/Downloads/sconjoint-fits")
```

Each chapter runs in its own R session. To render the book with the fits elsewhere, put that line
in an `.Rprofile` file in the book's folder.

```{r}
#| label: fits-check
fits <- getOption("sconjoint.fits", "fits")
file.exists(file.path(fits, c("gs_q3.rds", "br_q4.rds")))
gs <- sc_load(file.path(fits, "gs_q3.rds"))
gs
```

The printout gives the rank $q$, the number of folds, respondents and coded features, and the
integration settings used for the information and the scores. `sc_load()` returns `NULL` with a message when the
file is missing. It stops when the checksum does not match.
